title: The Human Body
intro: Bones, blood, muscles and more. Discover how your amazing body works.

questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood all around your body?
questions.explanation: Your heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of your body.

questions.prompt: About how many bones does an adult human skeleton have?
questions.explanation: An adult skeleton has 206 bones. Babies start with more, and some join together as they grow.

questions.prompt: Babies are born with more bones than adults have.
questions.explanation: Babies have around 300 bones or bone parts. Many of them fuse together as a child grows, leaving 206 in an adult.

questions.prompt: Which organs do you use to breathe?
questions.explanation: Your lungs take in oxygen from the air you breathe and get rid of carbon dioxide when you breathe out.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Your skin is your largest organ. It protects your body and helps keep you at the right temperature.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body sends and receives messages to control what you do?
questions.explanation: Your brain is the control centre of your body, sending and receiving messages through your nerves.

questions.prompt: Your heart is a muscle.
questions.explanation: The heart is made of a special kind of muscle that keeps squeezing to pump blood, without you having to think about it.

questions.prompt: When a child is resting, about how many times a minute does their heart beat?
questions.explanation: At rest, a child's heart usually beats between about 70 and 100 times a minute. Exercise makes it beat faster.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells pick up oxygen in the lungs and carry it around the body.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the smallest bone in the human body, found inside the ear?
questions.explanation: The stapes, also called the stirrup, sits deep inside your ear. It is smaller than a grain of rice and helps you hear.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur is your thigh bone. It is the longest and strongest bone, running from your hip to your knee.

questions.prompt: Which organs clean your blood and make urine?
questions.explanation: Your two kidneys filter waste and extra water out of your blood. That waste leaves your body as urine.

questions.prompt: In which part of the body is most food broken down and taken into the blood?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is a long, coiled tube. Most of the goodness from your food passes through its walls into your blood.

questions.prompt: What are the blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart called?
questions.explanation: Veins carry blood back to your heart. Arteries do the opposite job, carrying blood away from the heart.

questions.prompt: How many teeth does a full set of adult teeth have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.explanation: Adults can have 32 teeth. The last four, called wisdom teeth, often do not appear until the late teens or later.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body has an iris and a pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris is the coloured part of your eye, and the pupil is the dark circle in the middle that lets light in.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells help your body fight germs?
questions.explanation: White blood cells are like a tiny army. They find germs that get into your body and help destroy them.

questions.prompt: Which tiny parts of your blood stick together to help make a scab?
questions.explanation: When you cut yourself, platelets rush to the spot and clump together to plug the gap. This helps form a scab.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the dome-shaped muscle under your lungs that helps you breathe?
questions.explanation: Your diaphragm tightens and flattens to pull air into your lungs, then relaxes to push it back out.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest material in the human body?
questions.explanation: Enamel is the shiny outer coat of your teeth. It is harder than bone, which is why brushing to protect it matters.

questions.prompt: Where in your body would you find the snail-shaped cochlea?
questions.explanation: The cochlea is deep inside your ear. It is shaped like a snail shell and turns sound vibrations into signals for your brain.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest solid organ inside your body?
questions.explanation: Your liver sits under your ribs on the right side. It does hundreds of jobs, like storing energy and cleaning your blood.

questions.prompt: About how many muscles are in the human body?
questions.explanation: You have more than 600 muscles. They help you do everything from smiling and blinking to running and jumping.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the bony case that protects your brain?
questions.explanation: Your skull is made of bones that join together like a strong helmet, keeping your brain safe.

questions.prompt: What are the small bones that stack up to make your backbone called?
questions.explanation: Your backbone is a column of small bones called vertebrae. It lets you bend and twist while protecting the nerves inside.

questions.prompt: Your stomach makes acid to help break down food.
questions.explanation: Your stomach mixes food with strong acid and juices. This turns it into a thick mush before it moves on to your small intestine.

questions.prompt: Your hair and your fingernails are made of the same tough material, called keratin.
questions.explanation: Keratin is a strong protein. It makes up your hair and nails, and also animal horns, hooves and claws.

questions.prompt: The blood inside your veins is blue.
questions.explanation: Blood is always red. Veins can look blue through your skin because of the way light passes through it, but the blood itself is red.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of ribs do most people have?
questions.explanation: Most people have 12 pairs of ribs, making 24 ribs in all. They curve round like a cage to protect your heart and lungs.

questions.prompt: A healthy person's normal body temperature is about how many degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: Your body works best at around 37 °C. A temperature of 38 °C or more usually means you have a fever.
